note: FIVE VACUOUS GUARDS IN ONE CAMPAIGN, and the fifth was in the file whose own module doc lectures about the other four. The Millrace, all found and fixed in-flight. (1) A probe corroborated its transcription against channel-connectivity, which metrics.rs:7111 documents as CONSTANT at 1.0 since the confluence repair -- so any transcription, including a badly wrong one, printed the same number. (2) An index-vs-reference equality test detected a deleted pruning bound on exactly ONE probe in 6,175, and dropping its pole test entirely left it green. (3) A memo-exactness proof asserted per-run intactness vectors that are BOTH all-true on every world, because the column reads 1.0 everywhere -- replacing the memo body with vec of true left every world-level test green. (4) A doc comment claimed a future edit could not re-point the metric at the old rule; swapping the closure back left the test green. (5) The k-measurement probe took its oracle from nearest_line, which after the index landed IS the index -- so probe and index rested on the SAME inequality with the SAME L_max, and a wrong inequality would be agreed on rather than caught. THE COMMON SHAPE: an assertion whose reference is derived from the thing it is supposed to constrain. THE COMMON CURE, and it is cheap: mutate the thing the assertion is about and watch it redden. Every one of these five was found by a mutation, never by reading. Corollary learned at cost: when a column is a DOCUMENTED CONSTANT, nothing computed from it can corroborate anything -- assert on hop counts, verdict vectors or hand-built literals instead. And verify a revert by RE-RUNNING after touch, never by grepping source: a mv-style revert can restore an mtime older than the compiled binary, and the false-GREEN direction silently invalidates the whole proof.
